title: Coming Home to the House of the Lord
summary: One day we will cross the threshold of our real home, the house of the Lord, with a sigh of relief deeper than any earthly rest.
exhortation: I have a memory of staying at the house of a pastor who was a friend of mine. I went to church with him, mingled a bit afterward, and went back to his house ahead of him. Of course, he's the pastor, so he was there a lot longer. I was sitting in his living room when he got home, and he didn't see me right away. For some reason I'll never forget hearing him let out an involuntary sigh of relief as he crossed the threshold of his home. I don't even think he realized it. It was just his reaction to being home.

Maybe that sounds a bit random, but it was very profound to me. There's something about home. I know how it feels after a long day of work, when your body is just aching. You can't truly relax until you get home. There's a release of tension when you walk through that door. I love my home: my wife, my kids, my couch, my chair, my snacks, my coffee maker.

As Christians, this is what we're going to feel when we come to our real home. The house of the Lord will be a refuge of comfort and rest. Have you ever been on a long trip and been so excited to be home? One day we will dwell in the house of the Lord because of the mercy he has poured out on us through Jesus. We will have that sigh of relief. The tension will fall from our backs like a weighted vest, and we will sink into a rest far more delicious than any five-star resort could ever offer. Because this will be home: brand new, yet more familiar than our home now. Family, food, fellowship. We will be perfectly protected and perfectly at ease.

As we think about the wonderful future ahead of us, let it cause us to wonder at the great mercy and goodness of God: that he would come and rescue us, adopt us, and make us part of his home, that he would love us and make us part of his family so that we might be with him forever. And let it put a passion in our hearts to share the good news of God's love and mercy with those around us.
prayer: We long for that day, Lord. What a comfort going to our real home will be. What a great hope we have in you. We can walk through any trial and any loss with full and complete hope and trust in you, knowing that what awaits us is an eternal, glorious home that will far surpass every comfort we have ever experienced in our earthly homes.

All of those comforts are just echoes of a future so great and so wondrous that we can't even imagine it, with all the saints who have gone before us there to greet us. Thank you, Jesus, for this great hope you've called us to. Amen.
